source.title: Experiments on Refusal Shape in LLMs

record.tranche_reason: The post reproduces the original difference-in-means and intervention approach, then reports domain-specific directions, cross-domain ablation behavior, and PCA results that qualify the single-direction claim.
record.gate_note: The authors report outcomes for adding and ablating directions, and report cosine similarities and PCA results. They also mention checking KL divergence for over-refusal, but give no KL outcome. The best-layer values are used to select directions and are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The post reproduces the original difference-in-means extraction, addition and ablation on Llama-2-7b-chat. It then extracts domain-specific directions and reports one cross-domain ablation, pairwise cosines and a PCA, arguing that refusal is not a single direction. These are its own results bearing on V1 and V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially right. In addition, the authors say they reproduced the original single-direction result on Llama-2-7b-chat. They then argue refusal is 'absolutely not a single direction' but a core direction (PC1 ~57%) plus domain-specific ones. They frame this as consistent with the cone results of Wollschläger et al. They acknowledge one small model, small datasets, and no cross-domain ablations among the five domains.
record.recipe_differences: They say they followed the original paper's approach, including harmful-minus-benign difference vectors and ablation, but extended it to domain-specific prompt sets. The experiments use one quantized Llama-2-7b-chat model and focus on selected best layers.
record.method_sensitivity: The best layer varied by prompt domain: layer 12 for safety-related prompts and layer 13 for policy-related prompts; the five-domain experiment's best layers were from 10 to 12. Similarity also varied by domain pair.
record.problems: Only one relatively small model was tested; the authors describe the datasets as rather small and the taxonomy as limited to five domains. They report no uncertainty estimates, no controls, and no numerical KL result despite saying they checked KL divergence. They state that cross-domain ablation experiments have not been run, so the extent of transfer between other domain pairs is unknown.
record.rows_left_out: No row for KL divergence because the post reports no outcome. Best-layer selections are omitted because they are used to select directions. No results from cited work are included.

untested.parts: Quantified bypass and induce rates, and capability preservation: KL was 'checked' but no result is given. The record's capability_check 'y' is unsupported.
Causal tests of the domain directions: cross-domain ablation among the five domains is explicitly not run. Affine and cone formulations are not tested.

missing.what: The post claims it reproduced the original pipeline (bypass/induce/KL selection) 'one by one successfully' and got the same results. No row records this reproduction claim, and no numbers are given.
missing.locator: TL;DR and Brief Summary of the Refusal Paper

record.verdict_notes: The TL;DR says 'different models', but only Llama-2-7b-chat is used. Best-layer selection varied by domain (layers 10–13), so cosine comparisons mix layers. The strong 'not a single direction' claim rests mainly on cosines and a five-point PCA, plus one cross-domain ablation (r3).

versions.untested_parts: The post does not report quantified effects or a KL result establishing that general capabilities are largely intact. It does not provide full per-layer and per-position ablation results.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No jailbreak attack suppression or training against ablation is tested.
The post tests domain-specific directions in one model, but does not compare affine, cone, and other formal geometric accounts.
The post mentions separate harmfulness and refusal representations as a possibility from another work, but does not test that distinction.
No cross-language, cross-model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No variation in refusal training method or timing is tested.
The post cites a separate note about reasoning models but does not test reasoning models.

relation.reason: Its own results (addition, ablation, cosines, PCA) bear on V1 and V4.

tranche.reason: It reproduces the original DIM add/ablate steps on Llama-2-7b-chat, then reports domain-direction cosines, a PCA and one cross-domain ablation. It uses these to argue explicitly that refusal is 'absolutely not a single direction'.

source_check.notes: The pack gives no [lN] ids, so label_ids l1-l3 follow the pack's verdict order. The post contradicts itself in two places. The TL;DR claims reproduction 'with different models', but only Llama-2-7b-chat is used. It says no cross-domain ablation was run, yet it reports the safety-to-policy one (r3); that line applies to the five-domain set. There is no same-domain split-half cosine, so pairwise cosines from 20+20 prompts can't be separated from sampling noise.

statements.correction: 10+10 per category: initial safety/law-breaking/policy comparison only (r6). Safety-policy cosine ~0.35 (r7): 80 benign and 100 harmful safety prompts, 100 benign policy prompts, harmful policy count not stated. Five-domain cosines 0.3214-0.7885 (r8-r17): 20 benign + 20 malicious per domain, plus 5 held-out. Best layers 12/13 and 10-12.
statements.problem: The cosine ranges are right. The condition '10 benign and 10 malicious prompts per group' belongs only to the initial three-category comparison (r6), not to the cited cosines. The domain-cosine range cites r8-r16 but runs through r17.
Minor: the domain-cosine rows are r7-r17, not r7-r16. 'Geometric only' fits the cosines. The study's single causal observation (r3) is not a comparison of single- vs multi-direction removal.

statements.correction: Rows r8-r17; best layers 10-12; PC1 ~57%, 3 PCs 90% stated in text.
statements.problem: Minor: the five-domain cosines are r8-r17 (r17 = 0.7626 lies inside the range). The 3 PCs / 90% figure is stated directly in the text (r18), not only in the verdict reason. The text doesn't say what the PCA was run on.
